steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: Free Rania! Free all political prisoners!

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: Release the reserves! Share the energy! Heat for all the people!

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Excuse me, pardon me, let me pass...

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Zima! Istina! Where are you...?

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: Liberty for the people! Bread for the people!

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: Today's silence is tomorrow's slavery! Make our voices heard!

steps.name: Ursus Student
steps.text: Show yourselves! We demand parley!

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I believe those present know the rest better than I do.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: The ballroom was in chaos. In their panic, some attendees removed their gowns, snatched women's hats out of the servants' hands and ran outside...

steps.name: Angry Noble
steps.text: Preposterous! You weren't even at the ball! Who told you these rumors?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: They're all over the police force, and it's hard to tell where they come from. I offer you my apologies, if the rumors are unsubstantiated—

steps.name: Angry Noble
steps.text: Not me!

steps.name: Angry Noble
steps.text: N-Not to me! Apologize to everyone who was at the ball!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Order!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: This hearing is not interested in street rumors. It is what happened with the students that we wish to know.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: For example, who spoke those foul words of sedition?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Which words?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Which else? The foulest, most treacherous ones.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: People were saying all sorts of things. I'm not sure what you're referring to—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: The most treasonous, blasphemous, sacrilegious words... the ones that no one in this room may utter!

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Oh, I get it.

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Death to the mudak Emperor!

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Death to the mudak Emperor!

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Death to the mudak Emperor!

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Death to the mudak Emperor!

steps.name: Leonid
steps.text: Death to the Hippogryph-blooded filth! Ursus belongs to the Ursus!

steps.name: Angry Student
steps.text: Bring out the bloodsucker Witte! Bring out the imbecile Fyodor!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: You mean to say every student blasphemed against His Imperial Majesty that night.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Maybe, other than the few who kept cool heads. The young can be hot-blooded, and become incited to speak with a voice that does not belong to them.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Or perhaps you are exaggerating in order to cover up for a few of their number.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I am only telling the truth. You're jumping to some shocking conclusions.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Let us go back to the previous statement. You explained why Baryshnya Rostova failed to notice His Imperial Majesty's absence. Do you know where he was?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I learned a few things through my police contacts, but they are vague and uncertain.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: You know of his whereabouts?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I know he was in the palace, but not why he did not appear at the ball as scheduled.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: No, you know.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I'm sorry?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: My evidence indicates that the Deity Grypherburg Police Night's Watch was the first to learn of His Imperial Majesty's disappearance, which means that you, too, were in a position to know.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Answer, Young Zoya. Why are you hiding the truth about the attempt on the Emperor's life, and his subsequent disappearance during the protests in question?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: If you knew, your friend, Sonya Mykhailivna, knew too.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Was the violence that she incited in the quarantine zone aimed at finishing what the assassin attempt began?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: (Murmurs) So the Emperor went missing that night. That explains everything.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Natalya mentioned something in particular. Before the protests began, she was heading to where the chairman and vice chairman were, but her attention, like the others, was drawn to the light outside the window.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Both of them had left by the time she looked back.
Day of the hearing, a Tsarevgrad Office

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: If you don't want to appear at the hearing, I can go in your place, at least minimize the impact of the Emperor's disappearance by influencing the direction of the hearing.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: There is no longer a need to hide, Vasha.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Virtually every major noble in Grypherburg has learned about His Imperial Majesty's 'act of whimsy'. No number of gag orders will wipe away the shock that the event has caused.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Right now, I don't give two hoots about the hearing or the public opinion. The only thing on my mind is His Majesty's safety. You must find out what happened that day, before we move to eliminate the issues that put the Emperor in danger.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It was more than just Grypherburg's guards that went out of control that day. It was a warning sign, and a lesson to learn from.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Forgive my imprudence, Chairman Witte, but I understand that you had an argument with His Imperial Majesty prior to the ball, where he expressed his displeasure with the State Council's handling of the Katorga matter.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: If that is what you are referring to, people on the outside would not be surprised, for His Imperial Majesty is ever caring of all who walk upon this land, even if his kindness is often mistaken for weakness.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: No, not that.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: His Majesty was indeed in a bad mood, but he agreed to attend the ball, until I received a tip prior to the event—

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Someone was attempting to place an Originium bomb in the ballroom. He was caught by a maintenance worker.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Attempting to assassinate His Imperial Majesty?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It is not so simple. I thought the same as you did, so I followed emergency protocols and instructed the Royal Guard to go to His Majesty's chambers and escort him through the underground tunnel, while I interrogated the assassin personally.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: He claimed he was here to assassinate Baron Kamshalov, at the behest of the baroness.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: It would be a captivating family drama, if circumstances were different...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: As the interrogation continued, however, he mentioned something even more unsettling—

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Damn... come on, Geil, keep it together, you can do it...
Crouched on the floor, he wipes the sweat from his eyes, while haphazard parts are scattered across the red carpet.
A round 'alarm clock', three sticks of explosives bundled together like sausages, and numerous wires. A simple bomb that even a novice could assemble by following the instructions.
But the sweat has soaked through the paper he is holding, blurring the writing to illegibility.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Okay, I can still read this... connect the blue wire, then the green one, then a funt of... a funt of...

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: A funt of canned stew?

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Blyat! Ivan! The baroness paid so much, and you're passing off a recipe as bombmaking instructions?!

spans.text: Ivan! The baroness paid so much, and you're passing off a recipe as bombmaking instructions?!

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Alright, calm down, it's up to me now... maybe this green one goes into this connector.
Wrong, the green one goes below the blue one.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Let's give that a try...

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: It worked! Thank you, kind-hearted—

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Who the khuy are you?

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: (Hushed) Calm down and don't yell! Do you want to bring the whole police force down on our heads?

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: I had to stop you. If you really put that wire in, we'd have one more, no, two more 'canned stews' here in this room.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: Don't worry, we're fellow travelers, I'm not gonna sell you out.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: We're what?

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Are you in a noblewoman's pocket too?

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: What are you talking about? We're both assassins, aren't we?

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Sorry, I... it's my first time. I'm not really familiar with this stuff.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: Hey, everybody's gotta start somewhere. Who's your debut job? Is it a big one?

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: I don't know if he's big or not. All I know is that he's a baron with a casino.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: Well, that's not a bad one to pop your cherry. You'll get jobs for bigger fins with some practice under your belt.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: Heh, cover your mouth first. Don't want you freaking out and drawing unwanted attention.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: (Hushed) I'm here to kill Duchess Volkina.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Who's that?

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: You don't know her?!

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Quiet, quiet—

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: She's one of the few hereditary dukes in Ursus, a thorn in the side of the old guard nobility, and blood relative to the Emperor himself!

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Okay, okay, don't shout, I'm sorry...

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: My employer searched across all of Ursus for an assassin who could take the job, and I was the only one who would do it! How could you—

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: ...You—
Shh—

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: ...Shh?
The surprise visitor shakes his head and gestures to the table on the other side. The nervous assassin hesitates, then walks over slowly.
Give it to me.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: You want this bread?
The man shakes his head.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: Don't tell me you want the table knife?
The man nods.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: Wait, tell us what you're gonna do with it first. Giving a knife to a stranger is not exactly becoming of a professional assassin.
Give it to me, and I'll tell you.
The nervous assassin dares not approach. He tosses the knife to the man, who picks it up silently, then makes a sign with two fingers.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: Go out the door, go through the kitchen, climb the ladder to the roof, and get into the room on the west side via the sunroof.
Shh—

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: ...Shh.
The edge of the visitor's mouth twitches. He nods and departs, leaving behind the two stunned assassins.

steps.name: Nervous Assassin
steps.text: What were you talking about? I didn't understand a word.

steps.name: Relaxed Assassin
steps.text: He's here to kill... the Emperor.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: So you mean palace security allowed all these myriad assassins into the ballroom, and it took a maintenance worker to discover them.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: How many more surprises do the Grypherburg's guards have in store for us?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: The capital-wide power outage happened soon after.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: While not entirely unexpected, given the recent energy shortage, it coincided with the matter of the assassins, which led to an overreaction.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: That is why, after we left the scene of the ball, I instructed you to head to police headquarters and search for suspicious persons amongst the protestors.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You saw their crude, ineffective methods.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It's a good thing that your daughter is hardworking and motivated. If she was unambitious and went into the Guard by pulling strings, you would be the one with the constant headaches.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I am glad for Eloysius that you are willing to mentor her. Our entire family is very proud.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: But how could these absurdly incompetent assassins have affected His Imperial Majesty?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Do you remember who I sent to find him, according to emergency procedures?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: The Royal Guard?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: That's what I don't understand. Why would the Emperor need to flee, if he was protected by the Royal Guard?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: (Hushed) Because the loyalty of the Royal Guard is to Ursus, not the Emperor.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Why are you still here?
You're late, Witte.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: ...Where is His Imperial Majesty? Did you not go with him?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Your orders were to go to his room and guard against assassins.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I ordered you to protect the Emperor! This is a plan that's long been in place. In the event of any emergency, you are to personally escort him through the secret passage.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Unfortunately, your best intentions do not seem to be appreciated.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Do you mean...?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Have you not realized, Chairman?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: The one you're sworn to protect has been thoroughly disappointed by all that has happened here for years, decades even.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Of course, given your unreserved loyalty over such a long period of time, he would trust you, even if he sees all the other nobles as traitors.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: But he will not put the same trust in me.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What happened to His Majesty?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: He left by way of the secret passage, as planned, but he steadfastly refused my escort.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Didn't you stop him?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Why would I stop him?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You may not understand how I think, but you should try to understand how he thinks, 'Caretaker'.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Let him go out and see for himself what Ursus is truly like, beyond the window.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Which means that His Imperial Majesty has disappeared from under the watch of the Royal Guard.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Even if it was of his own volition.
The air itself seems thinner in the tightly packed formation of students, but they make room for their leader, Olga, giving a small but isolated space.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Fellow students! Unite and bring down the establishment!
The young noble lady stands proudly upon a battered oak casket, a faded family emblem faintly visible upon it.
Her shouting is drowned out by even more radical chants, but she squints as if to take in this Grypherburg night that belongs to them, until someone makes it to her side.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Time to put this to bed, Olga!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Sonya?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No marching, not even unified slogans... I see booze in the crowd. This is too risky.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Don't pour cold water when morale is at its highest—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Listen to me! These streets are lined with noble townhouses. Look how narrow the path is, it'd make any retreat really bad.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: More than that, I haven't seen a single cop.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: There's more to this than we know. Let's march south, shout our chants that way. It'll be easier to respond to any surprises.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I know what you're trying to say, but all this is normal. Faddey already explained that police operations are disrupted during the Winter Ball due to the personnel changes.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Besides, given our background, activism for our friends' rights, within reason, is seen as a sort of youthful experience, not rebellion.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Set your heart at ease and stand with us, Sonya.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Right... given your background.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: If you're gonna be stubborn about this, I'll have to take the SSG and go.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: This is not like you, Sonya. I thought you would be the bravest and firmest at a time like this.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: We have caught their attention and left an impression. All that is left is to negotiate for Rania's release, and enjoy the fruits of victory.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: If victory is so close, you can enjoy it yourself! No need to save any for me.
No sooner has she said these words than the ballroom's lights turn off, plunging the scene into darkness. Several screams can be heard from inside, then hushed conversations and sobbing.
The students fall silent, looking at each other in bewilderment. This is the quietest moment of this Grypherburg evening.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Did your group do this, Sonya?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: No, we didn't do anyth—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Beautifully done!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I'll pretend I didn't hear what you said before. The Self-Government Group has done a great service to our protest!
She pats Zima's shoulder excitedly. Zima hears a soft, indistinct sound coming from the end of the street, so quiet that it is almost drowned out by Olga's patting.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: ...Look out!
She pulls Olga and runs. A few black cans fall to the ground, leaving light tracks on the snow, before emanating a white smoke.
The nearest student screams, his voice rasping, before it is interrupted by violent coughing as sulfuric smoke attacks his eyes, nose and mouth like tiny gravel.
Then another, and another, as more students find their sight and breath stolen, screaming and twitching as they clutch at their faces. The others cry out in terror and disperse.
Many have fallen to the ground, calling for their friends in vain. They press their faces to the stone and hear the sound of approaching footsteps.
Tear gas deployed! Take the injured, leave the rest!
The late-arriving guardsmen raise their flashlights, casting powerful beams of light upon the young, frightened faces of the students.
The students that can still move run to the end of the street, crying and screaming, half-stumbling and half-crawling, their clothes soiled with muddy snow, footsteps, even blood.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: General! We're here!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Let's go! It's a mess back there!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Wait, where's Gummy?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: She went to look for you! Didn't you see her?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Blyat!
Zima turns and charges into the chaotic crowd without a second thought, ignoring the calls of Istina and Leto behind her.
It takes some time for her to get back to where Olga was, a scene of bedlam with guardsmen clubbing the remaining resisters with nightsticks.
Gummy is standing in front of Zima, slowly walking to a policeman, staring at his stick-wielding hand.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Why is Papa's watch here...?

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: What did you do to him?!

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: —Freeze! Get on your knees!
A nightstick swings for Gummy. She dodges instinctively and sees the man before her tackled to the ground by a black shadow, causing a slushy splash.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Zima?!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Run!

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Guardsman down! I need backup!

A dozen guardsmen rush in from every direction, grabbing Zima's shoulders and trying to separate her from their colleague on the ground, but she does not budge in the slightest. They begin striking her in the back with their nightsticks.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Gotcha, Gummy!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What are you doing? Get away from her!

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Chase them off. We're pulling out.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Sonya!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Have you lost your mind, Leto?!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Get out of here! That's an order!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hmph... not gonna happen!

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Zima! No, I'm helping you—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Don't try to be a hero, Sonya! Take our hands!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: You're out of your mind too? There's more of them back there, and they've got crossbows.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Retreat! That's an order!

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Don't try to pull rank with me! It won't work!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I need you to take them away, and the students out there need you! Help them!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: That's not an order then. It's a favor, from a friend!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Listen to me, just this once! Go—

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: ...And that's all that happened that night.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Some here may find it hard to accept, but Sonya should be considered a victim in this incident, regardless of which angle you take.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: The parliamentarian has noted the witness's account, which will be used in conjunction with the statement Zoya previously submitted to compile an official report.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Any further questions for the witness?

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: Your Honor, Young Zoya, perhaps some of us have misunderstood the purpose of the hearing.

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: The reason that many have called for the student groups' actions to recognized as treason is not the protest alone, but also their disruptive behavior in the quarantine zone.

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: Of foremost concern to us is this: Where was His Imperial Majesty Fyodor in the course of these events?

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: There have been various rumors running through the people, some claiming that His Majesty mobilized the students against the nobility.

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: I am therefore quite curious; for example, on the night of the protests, why did His Imperial Majesty—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Forgive the interruption, Count Troyan.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: I must emphasize that the Chairman will not be present today, in order to reduce the pressure on the committee, nor has he made any implicit suggestion.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: The reason I questioned the witness concerning His Imperial Majesty's whereabouts was only to understand the relationship between the attempted assassination, the Emperor's subsequent disappearance, and the actions of the student leader Sonya Mykhailivna.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: If the committee still has doubts, we can clarify them here and now.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Please answer, Young Zoya.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Do you think Sonya Mykhailivna's actions during the protest had anything to do with the assassination attempt on His Imperial Majesty or his disappearance?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: The decision of the Royal Guard...

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: The part that is most important, yet one that no one can know. It will not be part of the hearing's findings.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Did His Majesty say anything to you upon his return?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: No, Vasha, no...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: We can all see how taciturn he has become since.
